headline: Approved July minutes and tabled a membership item; discussed McKay School elevator repair and Main Street renovations.
summary: Facility staff at 96 Franklin Road agreed to stripe the area by a curb cut and add an HP parking space. The school district said the broken McKay School elevator will be replaced at an estimated cost of $1.5 million to $2.2 million over 12 to 18 months. Developers plan to ask the Architectural Access Board for waivers on 533 and 298 Main St., and they asked a member to walk through both properties.
decisions: Approved the July 2026 meeting minutes; motion passed.

CITY OF FITCHBURG 
FITCHBURG DISABILITY COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES 
 
1 
Fitchburg Disability Commission September 2026 Minutes 
 
 
 
MEETING DATE  September 9, 2026 
MEETING TIME:  9:30 AM 
LOCATION:   FITCHBURG CITY HALL, WEST ROOM 
MEMBERS PRESENT: Amy LeBlanc, DJ Tardiff,  Bill Tolos, Emily Stark, Tiffany Wells 
  
1. Approval of meeting minutes - Motion made and seconded to accept the minutes from our 
July 2026 meeting, motion passed. 
 
2. Events  
- Community Health Resource Fair is scheduled for September 24th from 4-7 PM at the 
armory.  Members needed to man our table. Carolyn will be hosting an art exhibit in the 
Fireplace room during the event. 
- Game Night is on for Thursday, October 8th, 2026, from 5pm - 7pm, at Seven Hills, 1460 
John Fitch Hwy, Fitchburg MA  01420.  People can register at  jdugas@sevenhills.org .  Amy 
will look into purchasing water and possibly food for the event.  DJ will develop a quick flyer. 
-Tiffany provided information on the following upcoming LUK sponsored events: 
There will be a zoom forum to discuss managing picky eating on Oct. 13th  and a Sensory 
Friendly Halloween Bash will be held on October 27th at the Elks – this is a family friendly 
event.  Folks can reach out to FamiliesConnected@luk.org or visit the LUK website for more 
details.  
 
3. Open Forum 
-Bill reported that he submitted a formal letter requesting an accommodation at the 
Fitchburg Art Community.  Currently signage is poor or lacking entirely indicating where 
packages are supposed to be left.  There are seven entrances – only one of which is fully 
accessible and packages are randomly left at all of the entrances making it difficult or 
impossible for residents to find and retrieve their deliveries. 
-DJ reported that they and CAP attended a 2-day Community Access Monitoring Training 
through MOD.  DJ found the handouts helpful but felt that the format was not very engaging. 
 
4. Resident Complaints and Concerns 
-The owner of 96 Franklin Road called promptly after receiving the letter the Commission 
sent regarding concerns with access to the property.  A time was set up for Amy to meet with 
facility staff at the site.  The staff agreed in the short-term to stripe the area in front of the 
existing curb cut to limit people parking there and blocking the ramp.  They also agreed to 
install an adjacent HP space with an upright sign and ground symbol.  Members will review 
the area prior to our next meeting to see if the initial work has been completed.  Long-term 
the owner’s representative was asked to consider a compliant ramp where currently a

crosswalk runs into the sidewalk adjacent to the building and to an additional HP space 
closer to the pizza place.   
 
-DJ spoke with Superintendent of Schools, John Thompson, about the broken elevator at 
McKay School and he provided the following information regarding this issue: 
 Fitchburg Public Schools (FPS) do not own McKay, they have a contract with Fitchburg State 
University (FSU)  to lease the building, 
 FPS has been working with FSU for some time on the elevator issue. 
 FSU has been working with Otis Elevator and authorized a number of repairs in an attempt to get 
the existing elevator back in service. Unfortunately, because of the age of the elevator and 
difficulty finding replacement parts, those repairs have not been successful.  
 In October 2025, Otis recommended a full system rebuild, which at the time was estimated at 
approximately $167,000, not including additional electrical and infrastructure work.  
 FPS have also talked with FSU about temporary accessibility solutions. Last year, we specifically 
asked them to look at whether a chair lift or stair lift could work while we waited for a permanent 
solution. Those options have  
 been explored, but we have since been told that the width and configuration of the stairwells 
make it difficult to install a lift that would meet accessibility requirements.  
 We raised the issue again this past June after hearing additional concerns from McKay staff. At 
that point, FSU had approximately $200,000 in other summer work planned for McKay and 
paused that work while looking at whether those resources could potentially be redirected 
toward the elevator.  
 FSU is now working with the state's Division of Capital Asset Management and Maintenance 
(DCAMM) on a full elevator replacement.  
 The current estimate we have been given for the replacement is approximately $1.5 million to 
$2.2 million, with a projected timeline of approximately 12 to 18 months.  
 Unfortunately, we have also been told that FSU does not anticipate the permanent solution being 
completed during this school year.  
 The length of that timeline concerns us, particularly when it comes to accessibility for our 
students, staff, families, and visitors. Because of these concerns, FPS  have reached out to our 
attorney, Marc Terry, and asked him to review the situation and our current agreement with 
Fitchburg State and advise us on what additional steps we should be considering while the 
permanent project moves forward.  
 In the mean-time services are maintained on the first floor as necessary without isolating any 
students or staff.  Affected families have been allowed transfers to other schools if they prefer. 
 
5. Review of Historic Main Street Properties undergoing renovation 
A tour of 533 Main St. and 298 Main St. with the developer will take place tomorrow.  Both of 
these historic properties have some tricky features that make full ADA compliance 
challenging or impossible.  They are planning request waivers from the Architectural Access 
Board.  They asked to meet and walk through the two properties with a Disability 
Commission member to demonstrate why waivers are needed, and if possible, get a letter 
concurring with the requests.
